sampling_model.design: Independent stratified sampling from \(E\) fixed environments with deterministic counts \(n_e\).
sampling_model.units: Within each environment, \((T_{e,i},Y_{e,i})_{i=1}^{n_e}\) are independent draws from \(P_e\), and samples are independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment is generated by \(T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e}\); there is no randomized assignment.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification comes from environmental cumulant shifts rather than treatment propensity overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cumulants through \(R_{\max}\) are estimated by symmetrized \(U\)-statistics, \(A\) by the rank-\(d\) SVD of \(\widehat C\), and the projected-moment influence covariance by leave-one-out first projections.  Independent Gaussian multipliers and vanishing Gaussian jitters provide the covariance-adaptive Anderson--Rubin calibration; reported coverage integrates over all auxiliary draws.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.6 proves that \(\beta\) is not identifiable from two environments when both \(\epsilon_u\) and \(\epsilon_t\) change.
Theorem 1 gives uniqueness of the BACKSHIFT joint diagonalizer if and only if every pair of intervention-variance profiles is nonproportional across environments.
Theorem 3.1 makes Causal Dantzig invariance identical to GMM moments, and regular GMM theory yields asymptotic normality and optimal weighting.
The paper's SR-AR and SR-CQLR tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength or moment-covariance eigenvalues.
Causal Dantzig identifies a linear causal coefficient through an invertible covariance-difference moment and gives regular low-dimensional confidence intervals.
Under perfect interventions, one intervention on each latent node is sufficient and worst-case necessary for coupled-cumulant recovery of linear causal disentanglement parameters.
Higher-order cumulants identify latent-variable LiNGAM effects when a proxy or underspecified instruments provide auxiliary source information.
The paper characterizes bivariate effect identifiability by exogenous-noise Gaussianity without auxiliary variables.

body.tldr: In a new low-rank population submodel of simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise shifts, any finite projected cumulant breakout identifies the structural effect, even above the inference order cap, while the bounded no-breakout branch retains an exact legal source-label ambiguity. A three-environment construction shows that every pair can remain source-swap ambiguous although the joint orthogonal flag identifies. On each first-breakout shell of every fixed admissible bounded model, the theory gives estimator-risk and conservative expected-length upper bounds; conservative coverage and asymptotically exact externally randomized calibration extend over the whole bounded class. Matching minimax lower bounds are established on one fixed compatible experiment.

project_justification.gap: The closest higher-moment result of Kivva et al. establishes a simultaneous-shift obstruction in a two-environment setting. It does not identify effects in arbitrary simultaneous-shift models, and its obstruction transfers here only on the explicitly constructed pairwise intersection. Covariance-based multi-environment methods impose different diagonal-shift geometry and do not supply the treatment-versus-latent source-label frontier studied here.
project_justification.niche: A newly imposed rank-\(d\) latent cumulant-profile plane creates a joint environmental direction that can be invisible in every pairwise reduction. Its first orthogonal breakout separates broad population identification from exact bounded-class source ambiguity and also serves as the statistical strength parameter.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an explicit observed-law quotient for every finite breakout in the broad all-orders population flag class, a legal-swap if-and-only-if frontier on the bounded domain, and a compound-Poisson \(d=1,E=3\) witness with pairwise ambiguity but joint rescue. It also gives the sharp environment and moment-order constructions, estimator and conservative interval upper bounds for every fixed admissible bounded model, matching lower bounds on one fixed compatible experiment, a uniform same-sample generated-projector expansion, and an externally randomized Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin calibration valid through singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance.

body.related_work: Kivva, Akbari, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2025), especially Theorem 3.6 and its source-swap argument, provide the closest two-environment simultaneous-shift obstruction and motivate the pairwise comparison. Their positive-radius local analytic moment condition implies the all-integer-order moment condition maintained here; global real-mgf finiteness is not needed. The present result concerns a new calibrated low-rank multi-environment submodel and does not claim positive identification for arbitrary simultaneous shifts in their published class. The obstruction is asserted to transfer only on the explicit pairwise intersection certified by the three-environment construction. Rothenhäusler, Heinze, Peters, and Meinshausen (2015) give BACKSHIFT's contrasting covariance joint-diagonalization condition, not the present profile, rank, or gap restrictions. Cai et al. (2023), Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025), and Tramontano et al. (2025) study higher-cumulant recovery under other latent, intervention, proxy, or instrumental structures. Long et al. (2023) provide an environmental GMM template, while Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) concern singularity-robust testing for supplied moments rather than the present generated cumulant plane. Davis and Kahan (1970) support spectral-projector perturbation only. Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (2020) document complications in the Sachs setting, and Sachs et al. (2005) supply the multi-perturbation application rather than evidence that the new profile condition holds.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The statistical results remain fixed-dimensional and use the bounded subclass's \(2R_{\max}+\delta\) envelope, balanced shares, fixed calibration gap, and fixed order cap. The deterministic Anderson--Rubin interval is conservative over every fixed admissible bounded \(\Theta\). The covariance-adaptive refinement is asymptotic and its exact coverage is unconditional over the data and all external Gaussian and Monte Carlo draws; it does not promise finite-sample exactness, conditional-on-randomization coverage, or deterministic threshold calibration at an atom. Matching full-observation minimax lower bounds are proved only on one fixed compatible experiment. No expected-length or diameter optimality is claimed for \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\).
body.honest_scope: Population identification is proved only in the new all-orders low-rank flag class \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), not for arbitrary simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise shifts. The if-and-only-if statement is confined to the bounded legal-swap union \(\mathcal D_\rho\), whose no-breakout branch requires both source labelings to remain interior. The three-environment witness shows a genuine pairwise intersection with the Kivva et al. obstruction, but does not embed their whole published class. The explicit no-breakout and lower-bound constructions require compatible choices of coefficient, moment, and singular-gap bounds. A finite scan through \(R_{\max}\) cannot certify global no-breakout, although any later finite population breakout remains identifying. Estimator-risk and conservative expected-length upper bounds are universal over each fixed admissible bounded \(\Theta\), whereas matching minimax lower bounds are established only on one fixed compatible experiment. The randomized-jitter interval has asymptotically exact unconditional coverage over the bounded class, including no-breakout laws, but no expected-length or diameter optimality claim. The Sachs data motivate the consumer and do not verify the profile restriction.
